hook: SCP-1921 is a fire-damaged cotton candy stand found among signs for Herman Fuller's Circus of the Disquieting. Its candy is black, it settles into the brain, and a calliope on the back decides what happens next. The core of the article is a table of music rolls, so read the handwritten notes as carefully as the effects. Some of those effects involve force-feeding and death by seizure.
whyItMatters: It carries the herman-fuller and sugarcomb-confectionery tags, tying it to the circus named on the recovered signs and to the nonexistent candy maker on its label. It shows that circus at work through equipment rather than performers: each song's effect plus a scribbled note sketches how the show handled crowds, police and anyone who started asking questions. It is a neat example of telling a story through an inventory.
thingsToNotice:
Read the notes in order and the method comes into view: a main roll that makes anomalies seem normal, one aimed at police, one for when someone catches on, an emergencies-only roll that has subjects force candy on others, and a last-resort roll that kills listeners of cardiac arrest while they grow more cheerful. The tenth roll does nothing at all but tells someone to prepare the clowns for milking, which casts the black liquid in the tank labelled Clown Milk in a new light.

The restored ninth roll gives the real twist: in one test the calliope abandons its roll for a slowed Entrance of the Gladiators, the subject announces that he loves clowns, seizes and later wakes with no memory of who he is, and an autopsy finds a glitter-filled balloon in his chest wrapped around a folded note. The note reads as if someone was watching the machine misfire, asking if the contraption broke again and signing off to Charley about getting hungry. The six burned bodies stacked in the tent at the discovery site are never explained.
